rounds.text: Anand Rayons presents a compelling value proposition, trading at a P/E of 8.6, a price-to-book ratio of 0.92x, and an EV/EBITDA of 6.77x, all of which represent significant discounts to sector benchmarks of 17.52x, 1.29x, and 9.73x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7, E11, E53]. This valuation is particularly striking given the company's explosive growth, with trailing twelve-month profit increasing by 105% and sales by 42%, far outstripping the sector median profit growth of 20.0% and sales growth of 8.0% [E19, E16, E67, E68]. The market's current pricing implies a future earnings contraction of -3.8%, yet the company has delivered a consistent 59% profit CAGR over the last five years [E41, E17, E55]. Furthermore, the stock offers a substantial 79.1% margin of safety based on a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 209 per share [E39, E40]. It is conceded: [E34], [E35], [E32], and [E30] that the company faces high leverage and rising borrowings, yet the recent 0.95% increase in promoter holding suggests internal confidence at these levels [E56]. The company's fundamentals are significantly outpacing its stock price, as five-year profit grew 59% while the price grew only 2% [E50, E20]. This disconnect is further highlighted by an ROA of 7.1%, an ROE of 7.1%, and an ROCE of 8.71% that all outperform sector benchmarks, while the share price sits -90.9% away from its 52-week high and 0% of the way up its 52-week range despite new capacity coming online [E8, E9, E10, E43, E42, E36].

Anand Rayons Ltd presents severe fundamental and technical deterioration, evidenced by a dismal rules-based screen score of 32 out of 100 which firmly assigns a sell rating with low confidence [E61]. The stock is in freefall, sitting a mere 1% above its 52-week range low and resting below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E5, E44]. Furthermore, the company suffers from a total collapse in cash generation, posting a negative operating cash flow of Rs -11 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -14 Cr in March 2026, leading to a catastrophic cash conversion ratio of -1.57x [E30, E31, E32]. This severe cash burn is accompanied by a massive surge in borrowings to Rs 36 Cr in March 2026, up from Rs 16 Cr a year prior, worsening its historical high-leverage profile [E35, E34]. Insider confidence is also evaporating, with promoter holdings plunging by 17.20 percentage points from 70.72% in December 2023 down to 53.52% in July 2026 [E37]. Compounded by an abysmal relative-strength rating of 0 against the Nifty 500 and a brutal 12-month price return of -85.6%, the technical and operational risks are glaring [E45, E46]. Conceded: the company displays strong historical profit growth figures and trades at low multiples such as a P/E of 8.6x and a P/B of 0.92x [E1, E2, E19, E55].

Conceded: the rules-based screen scores 32 out of 100 [E61], the stock sits near its 52-week low below its moving averages [E5, E44], borrowings rose to Rs 36 Cr [E35], and promoter holding declined to 53.52% [E37]. However, the bear ignores that this very drop has created a stark disconnect between surging fundamentals and share price [E50]. Profit growth has vastly outpaced the 5-year price growth [E50], with trailing twelve-month profit growth reaching an extraordinary 105% [E19]. Furthermore, despite the negative cash flow in March 2026 [E31], the DCF intrinsic value calculation points to an immense margin of safety of 79.1% [E40]. The reverse DCF demonstrates that the current market price absurdly prices in a -3.8% earnings growth rate, completely ignoring the base case expectation of 18.0% [E41]. Finally, recent insider activity shows renewed commitment with promoter holding increasing by 0.95% over the last quarter [E56], alongside positive expectations for upcoming quarterly results [E54].

Conceded: profit growth reached 105% over the trailing twelve months [E19], and promoters increased holdings by 0.95% over the last quarter [E56]. However, the bull's reliance on a 79.1% margin of safety and a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 209 [E39, E40] ignores the immediate operational reality of negative cash flows, including an operating cash flow of Rs -11 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -14 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32]. The claim that the market absurdly prices in -3.8% earnings growth [E41] dismisses valid structural concerns, such as the rules-based screen scoring a failing 32 out of 100 [E61], a relative-strength rating of zero [E45], and severe price erosion with the stock sitting -90.9% away from its 52-week high [E43]. Furthermore, while promoters added shares last quarter [E56], the broader multi-year picture shows a substantial decline in promoter ownership from 70.72% in December 2023 down to 53.52% [E37], alongside a secular drop of -16.3% over the last three years [E60]. Finally, borrowings have doubled to Rs 36 Cr [E35], and debtor days have worsened to 73.0 days [E59], providing sound empirical justification for why the stock trades below its moving averages [E44] rather than representing a simple disconnect between fundamentals and price [E50].
